## HBR's Framework for Managing AI Agents

Harvard Business Review has published a critical framework for managing AI agents as organizational talent rather than software tools — with structured job descriptions, human oversight, contextual encoding, and performance governance. The core thesis is that AI agents should be managed like co-workers, not like software tools.

## Key Management Elements

Each agent requires a formal role definition that outlines its responsibilities, decision-making boundaries, and mandatory escalation points to human supervisors. Additionally, agents deliver the greatest value when assigned to tedious, repetitive, or cognitively draining tasks that currently frustrate employees — not necessarily the tasks that appear easiest to automate.

## Leadership Skills for AI Agents

# The Employee-Development Angle of AI Agents (2025–2026)

**Scope note on sourcing:** all claims below are tied to a URL. Items I could only partially verify are explicitly flagged. Fetched-and-read sources are marked; others are from search-result snippets (medium confidence).

## 1. L&D products that involve agents

The dominant pattern: **AI agents are used to deliver learning, or courses teach ABOUT agents.** Almost none frame everyday agent-work itself as development.

- **Sana Labs** — AI-native learning platform (Sana Learn) plus a separate agent platform (Sana Agents); acquired by Workday for ~$1.1B, completed Nov 4, 2025 (https://newsroom.workday.com/2025-11-04-Workday-Completes-Acquisition-of-Sana). Josh Bersin notes the strategic point is that Sana Agents connect to Sana Learn so "training or enablement is immediately integrated" (https://joshbersin.com/2026/03/workday-and-sana-unveil-a-bold-new-strategy-for-ai/). Framing: agents deliver learning — not "using agents develops you."
- **Degreed** — Vision 2025 launched **Degreed Maestro** (adaptive role-play, coaching, real-time skill feedback, integrated July 2025) and an **MCP server** delivering skills/role/learning context into tools like Microsoft Copilot — i.e., "agentic development experiences" (https://degreed.com/experience/newsroom/degreed-vision-2025-the-future-of-workforce-learning/, https://degreed.com/experience/blog/degreed-maestro-ai-purpose-built-for-learning/). Degreed's acquisition of Learn In (academies/upskilling-finance) is covered at https://clo100.com/2025/12/05/degreed-acquires-learn-in-implications-for-upskilling-platforms-and-how-ai-first-programmes-lead-the-way/. The MCP angle is notable: it pushes L&D context *into* the agent, adjacent to but not the same as crediting agent-work as development.
- **Multiverse** — pivoted to "Upskilling platform for AI adoption" (https://www.multiverse.io/); committed to 15,000 AI apprenticeships over two years, UK Growth and Skills Levy-funded, starting June 2025 (https://tech.eu/2025/06/09/multiverse-powers-national-ai-drive-with-15-000-new-apprenticeships/). Claims "agentic AI experts" as an outcome and cites 45% of learners earning promotions (https://www.multiverse.io/solutions/ai). This is the strongest *apprenticeship-as-career-development* framing, but the development mechanism is a formal program, not agent use itself.
- **Section (now sectionai.com)** — enterprise AI training with **ProfAI / "Section Coach"**, an AI coach that trains employees on prompting, use-case discovery, responsible use (https://www.sectionai.com/ai/profai, https://prof.ai/); issues Credly badges like "Section Coach: Basic AI Proficiency" (https://www.credly.com/org/section/badge/section-profai-ai-proficiency); advanced courses cover building Copilot Agents/Custom GPTs/Gemini Gems (https://www.sectionai.com/courses). Interesting recursion: an AI agent coaching you on AI skill — closest of the L&D vendors to "the agent develops the employee," but the agent is a dedicated tutor, not your work agent.
- **Uplimit** — sells three families of AI learning agents (skill-building, program-management, teaching-assistant agents); customers incl. GE Healthcare, Kraft Heinz; claims >90% completion (https://venturebeat.com/ai/uplimit-raises-stakes-in-corporate-learning-with-suite-of-ai-agents-that-can-train-1000-employees-simultaneously, https://uplimit.com/blog/uplimit-s-ai-learning-agents-drive-faster-skill-building-and-engagement). Again: agents deliver training.
- **Coursera** — many courses ABOUT building/managing agents: Microsoft AI Agents Professional Certificate ("build, deploy, and manage AI agents") (https://www.coursera.org/professional-certificates/microsoft-ai-agents), IBM RAG and Agentic AI (https://www.coursera.org/professional-certificates/ibm-rag-and-agentic-ai), Vanderbilt's AI Agent Developer (https://www.coursera.org/specializations/ai-agents), and a leader-oriented "Agentic AI and AI Agents for Leaders" specialization (https://www.coursera.org/specializations/ai-agents-for-leaders). Udemy equivalents exist ("Agentic AI for Leaders: Orchestrating Human + Machine Teams", https://www.udemy.com/course/agentic-ai-for-leaders-orchestrating-human-machine-teams/). I did not verify a LinkedIn-Learning-branded "manage your agent" flagship course — uncertain, treat as unconfirmed.
- **Anthropic "AI Fluency"** — free course + framework (with Ringling College / University College Cork) built on the **4Ds: Delegation, Description, Discernment, Diligence** (https://anthropic.skilljar.com/ai-fluency-framework-foundations, https://aifluencyframework.org/, https://www.coursera.org/learn/ai-fluency-framework-foundations). Significant because it names **delegation to AI** as a formal, teachable competency — the clearest canonical "managing AI is a skill" curriculum.
- **Microsoft Learning Agent** — a Copilot agent for "personalized AI upskilling for every employee," now GA, with learning streaks and reporting via the Viva Insights Agent Dashboard (https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoft365copilotblog/learning-agent-now-generally-available-%E2%80%94-personalized-ai-upskilling-for-every-em/4524571). **Caveat:** the full page didn't render in my fetch; details (streaks, dashboards) come from the search snippet — medium confidence.

## 2. Explicit "managing agents is a skill / career move" framing

This framing is now mainstream in thought-leadership, and it's the strongest part of the landscape.

- **Microsoft Work Trend Index 2025 — "Frontier Firm" and "agent boss"** (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/worklab/work-trend-index/2025-the-year-the-frontier-firm-is-born, https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2025/04/23/the-2025-annual-work-trend-index-the-frontier-firm-is-born/). Key language: the agent boss "builds, delegates to, and manages agents to amplify their impact… **taking control of their career in the age of AI**"; every worker should "think like the CEO of an agent-powered startup." Stats: 28% of managers considering hiring AI workforce managers; 32% plan to hire AI agent specialists in 12–18 months; 36% of leaders expect managing AI systems in their scope within five years. This is the single most explicit "agent management = career development" artifact — but it's a research narrative, not a product.
- **Microsoft Work Trend Index 2026** (fetched: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/worklab/work-trend-index/agents-human-agency-and-the-opportunity-for-every-organization) — introduces "Frontier Professionals" who deliberately pause to decide what goes to AI vs. humans (53% vs 33% of average users); 86% of AI users treat AI output as a starting point; quality control of AI output and critical thinking named top skills; cites LinkedIn's 2026 Labor Market Report finding 1.3M+ AI-related job opportunities.
- **Ethan Mollick, "Management as AI superpower"** (fetched: https://www.oneusefulthing.org/p/management-as-ai-superpower) — argues management skill is the key competency for agent work ("If you can explain what you need, give effective feedback, and design ways of evaluating work, you are going to be able to work with agents"). Notably, Mollick argues the arrow points from existing management skill → agent effectiveness, **not** that agent work develops you.
- **Academic anchor:** Weidmann, Xu & **Deming**, "Measuring Human Leadership Skills with AI Agents," **NBER WP 33662** (fetched: https://www.nber.org/digest/202507/leadership-skills-managing-ai-agents-vs-humans) — leadership effectiveness with AI agent teams correlates 0.81 with effectiveness leading human teams (0.69 controlling for hard skills); AI-based leadership assessment cost $23 vs $114 per participant. This is the empirical bridge for "managing agents ≈ managing people" — and it explicitly suggests agent-management could be used to *assess* (and by extension develop) leadership. No commercial product built on it yet, as far as I found.
- **HBR:** "Agentic AI Is Already Changing the Workforce" (May 2025, https://hbr.org/2025/05/agentic-ai-is-already-changing-the-workforce) and "Create an Onboarding Plan for AI Agents" (March 2026, https://hbr.org/2026/03/create-an-onboarding-plan-for-ai-agents) — manage agents like teammates: role definitions, escalation points, coaching, "informed trust." Secondary commentary: https://www.aigovernancetoday.com/news/hbr-managing-ai-agents-coworkers-governance-2026 (blog, lower confidence).
- **McKinsey:** "The agentic organization" and "Rethink management and talent for agentic AI" (https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/people-and-organizational-performance/our-insights/the-agentic-organization-contours-of-the-next-paradigm-for-the-ai-era, https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/people-and-organizational-performance/our-insights/the-organization-blog/rethink-management-and-talent-for-agentic-ai) — calls for "agentic AI literacy," new roles (agent orchestrators, human-in-the-loop designers), and says the edge goes to people who combine domain expertise with "fluency in guiding agentic systems." Also "Building and managing an agentic AI workforce" (https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/people-and-organizational-performance/our-insights/the-future-of-work-is-agentic).
- **Fortune** on managers learning to lead agents as a new accountable skill (Sept 2025): https://fortune.com/2025/09/05/managers-get-ready-learn-new-skill-leading-ai-agents-bots/
- **Job postings:** "AI agent manager" as a literal title exists mostly as aggregator categories (https://www.indeed.com/q-ai-agent-manager-jobs.html). What's real per secondary analysis: AI Operations Lead ($155k–$275k), AI Product Manager (Agents), and consulting roles governing "Copilots and autonomous agents" at Anthropic, Salesforce, EY, Deloitte, Accenture per https://theaicareerlab.com/blog/agentic-ai-jobs-guide-2026 (blog — medium confidence). Salesforce's own leadership piece: https://www.salesforce.com/blog/ai-workforce-management/.

## 3. Gamification / per-employee skill tracking through agent use

- **Salesforce Trailhead "Agentblazer" status** — the clearest productized, gamified agent-skill ladder: Champion → Innovator → Legend tiers (2026 version), badges and points on your public Trailblazer profile, Legend requiring a proctored Agentforce/AI Specialist cert, renewed annually (https://trailhead.salesforce.com/agentblazer, https://www.salesforce.com/blog/new-agentblazer-status/, https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/trails/become-an-agentblazer-legend-2026). Still credentialing *learning about* agents, though tied to hands-on agent building.
- **Bryq AI Fluency assessment** — scenario-based per-employee scoring (0–100) on five dimensions: task strategy, prompting, critical evaluation, ethical use, workflow integration (https://www.bryq.com/product/ai-fluency). The closest thing I found to a "prompt-skill score" product. (Snippet-verified; medium confidence on details.)
- **Gloat Skill Validation Agent** — gamified <5-min validations feeding internal talent-marketplace matching (https://gloat.com/use-cases-agents/skill-validation-agent/).
- **Microsoft Copilot Dashboard / Viva Insights benchmarks** (Oct 2025) — per-cohort AI adoption metrics, internal comparisons by manager/region/function and external benchmarks vs. top-10%/25% of peer companies (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/viva/insights/org-team-insights/copilot-dashboard, https://www.theregister.com/2025/10/10/microsoft_copilot_viva_insights/). This is "AI maturity dashboards" in practice — adoption surveillance, not skill development; press framed it as "your boss's favorite snitch" (https://www.windowscentral.com/artificial-intelligence/microsoft-copilot/copilot-viva-insights-benchmarks).
- **Duolingo-for-AI apps exist:** **Iro AI** literally markets itself as "The Duolingo for AI" — streaks, XP, duels, graded prompt-writing, 345 lessons including paths on *agents, automation, and managers* (https://tryiro.com/). **AILE** — gamified lessons, capability map, verifiable credentials (https://www.learnaile.com/). Consumer-grade, not enterprise; the "agents" path in Iro is the nearest thing to Duolingo-for-agent-management. (Both snippet-verified; medium confidence.)
- **Performance-review-as-incentive:** Shopify's April 2025 Lütke memo made AI use mandatory and put it into performance and peer reviews — "Using AI well is a skill that needs to be carefully learned by using it a lot" (https://www.forbes.com/sites/douglaslaney/2025/04/09/selling-ai-strategy-to-employees-shopify-ceos-manifesto/, https://www.firstround.com/ai/shopify). Duolingo announced the same (Apr 2025) then **rolled it back by April 2026** (https://fortune.com/2026/04/13/duolingo-ceo-luis-von-ahn-ai-usage-requirement-employee-performance-evaluations/). IgniteTech reportedly laid off ~80% for not adapting to AI (https://fortune.com/2025/08/18/duolingo-ceo-admits-controversial-ai-memo-did-not-give-enough-context-insists-company-never-laid-off-full-time-employees/ context; Washington Post overview: https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2025/06/03/ai-workplace-duolingo-shopify-employees/).

## 4. Verdict: largely whitespace

**Confirmed and crowded:** (a) courses/certs ABOUT agents (Coursera, Udemy, Section, Trailhead, Anthropic AI Fluency); (b) agents that DELIVER training (Sana, Uplimit, Degreed Maestro, Microsoft Learning Agent, Section ProfAI); (c) rhetoric that agent management is a career skill (Microsoft "agent boss," McKinsey, HBR, Mollick); (d) blunt incentives (Shopify reviews, Copilot adoption dashboards).

**Whitespace — no one found productizing "the agent-work itself develops the employee":** I found no product that treats an employee's real, day-to-day delegation to their own work agents as a development curriculum — e.g., scoring your actual delegation/feedback/verification behavior over time, mapping it to a management-competency ladder, feeding it into career progression. The pieces all exist separately:

- The **science** says agent management predicts human-leadership skill (Deming/Weidmann/Xu, NBER 33662) and even proposes agents as cheap leadership assessments — unproductized.
- The **framework** exists (Anthropic's 4Ds name Delegation/Discernment as competencies) — taught as a course, not measured in live agent work.
- The **telemetry** exists (Copilot Dashboard) — used for adoption benchmarking, not employee growth.
